outputs.L3:
The resin binder composition for toner contains a polyester resin obtained by polycondensing polyethylene terephthalate, a carboxylic acid component, and an alcohol component. In this composition, the polyethylene terephthalate used as a raw material has an intrinsic viscosity, or IV value, of 0.40 or more and 0.75 or less. By selecting polyethylene terephthalate within this IV range, the resulting polyester resin can be made suitable for use as a toner binder while maintaining desirable resin properties.

The alcohol component used in the polycondensation reaction contains, in an amount of 40% to 100% by mol, an aliphatic diol having 2 to 4 carbon atoms and having a hydroxyl group bonded to a secondary carbon atom. This specific alcohol component contributes to the structure and performance characteristics of the polyester resin, making it particularly useful in toner applications.

The invention also includes a method for producing the polyester resin contained in the resin binder composition. In this method, polyethylene terephthalate having an IV value of 0.40 to 0.75 is polycondensed together with the carboxylic acid component and the alcohol component described above, thereby forming the polyester resin used as the toner binder.

The resulting resin binder composition is suitable for electrophotographic toners. Such toners can be used for developing latent images in electrostatic image development processes, as well as in recording and printing methods. Accordingly, the composition is useful in applications such as electrophotographic copying machines, laser printers, and other image-forming devices that employ toner-based image development.
outputs.L4:
A resin binder composition for an electrophotographic toner is provided. The composition contains, as a principal binder component, a polyester resin obtained by polycondensing polyethylene terephthalate with a carboxylic acid component and an alcohol component. The alcohol component includes a substantial proportion of an aliphatic diol having a specific secondary-carbon structure, thereby imparting desirable physical and thermal properties to the resulting polyester resin.

The polyester resin produced in this manner is useful as a binder resin for toner particles employed in electrophotographic processes. By incorporating recycled or depolymerized polyethylene terephthalate as a raw material and combining it with selected acid and alcohol components, the resin can be designed to provide appropriate softening behavior, compatibility with colorants and additives, and performance suitable for fixing toner images onto recording media.

A toner prepared using this resin binder composition may further contain conventional toner ingredients, such as a colorant, a charge control agent, a release agent, and other optional additives. The binder resin supports stable dispersion of these components and contributes to the formation of toner particles having suitable charging characteristics, durability, and fixing performance.

The toner is suitable for use in the development of electrostatic latent images in electrophotographic apparatuses, including copying machines, printers, facsimile machines, and multifunction image-forming devices. In operation, the toner adheres to an electrostatic latent image formed on an image-bearing member, thereby developing the latent image into a visible toner image. The visible image can then be transferred to a recording medium, such as paper or film, and fixed by heat, pressure, or a combination thereof.

Because the binder composition is based on a polyester resin formed from polyethylene terephthalate and a selected secondary-carbon aliphatic diol-containing alcohol component, it can provide a favorable balance of toner properties, including image developability, fixability, storage stability, and resistance to offset during fixing. Accordingly, the resin binder composition is well suited for toners used in electrostatic image development, recording, and printing applications.
outputs.L5:
**The Power of “The”**

“The” is one of the smallest words in the English language, yet it is also one of the most important. It is called a definite article, and its main purpose is to point to something specific. When we say “a book,” we may mean any book, but when we say “the book,” we mean a particular book that the speaker and listener understand.

The word “the” helps make communication clearer. It tells us that something is already known, unique, or being identified directly. For example, “the sun” refers to the one sun in our solar system, while “the teacher” may refer to a specific teacher in a classroom or conversation.

Although “the” is short and often unnoticed, it appears constantly in everyday speech and writing. It connects ideas, gives precision, and helps organize meaning. Without it, English would sound incomplete and less natural.

In many ways, “the” proves that even the smallest words can have a powerful role in language.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent-style abstract for a resin binder composition for electrophotographic toner using recycled polyethylene terephthalate, specifying IV value ranges and alcohol component requirements.
counterfactuals.output: A resin binder composition for an electrophotographic toner is provided, the composition comprising a polyester resin obtained by reacting recycled polyethylene terephthalate with an alcohol component and an acid component. The recycled polyethylene terephthalate has an intrinsic viscosity (IV) of about 0.45 to about 0.85 dL/g, preferably about 0.50 to about 0.75 dL/g, as measured in a phenol/tetrachloroethane mixed solvent. The alcohol component comprises at least one diol selected from ethylene glycol, propylene glycol, neopentyl glycol, and bisphenol A alkylene oxide adducts, and contains, based on total alcohol component, about 20 to about 100 mol% of a C2-C6 aliphatic diol and about 0 to about 80 mol% of an aromatic diol component. The resin binder composition provides a toner having improved low-temperature fixability, storage stability, and charge stability while enabling effective reuse of polyethylene terephthalate waste.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a concise invention summary describing a toner binder composition containing a polyester resin made from PET, a carboxylic acid component, and an alcohol component, including suitable applications in electrostatic image development.
counterfactuals.output:
An invention is provided for a toner binder composition comprising a polyester resin obtained by reacting polyethylene terephthalate (PET) with a carboxylic acid component and an alcohol component. The PET may be virgin, recycled, or waste PET, enabling effective reuse of polyester materials while providing a binder resin suitable for toner performance requirements.

The carboxylic acid component may include aromatic or aliphatic dicarboxylic acids, acid anhydrides, or ester-forming derivatives, and the alcohol component may include diols, polyols, or alkylene oxide adducts. By selecting the acid and alcohol components, the polyester resin can be tailored to provide desirable softening temperature, glass transition temperature, melt viscosity, chargeability, fixability, and storage stability.

The toner binder composition may be blended with conventional toner additives, such as colorants, charge control agents, waxes, release agents, magnetic materials, and external additives, to form toner particles. The composition is suitable for use in toners for electrostatic image development, including electrophotographic printers, copiers, facsimile machines, and multifunction devices, and may be used in both monochrome and full-color toner formulations.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a Japanese patent abstract in English for a polyester resin binder for toner, where the PET has an intrinsic viscosity of 0.40–0.75 and the alcohol component includes 40–100 mol% of an aliphatic secondary diol with 2–4 carbon atoms.

**Abstract**

**PROBLEM TO BE SOLVED:** To provide a polyester resin binder for toner which gives a toner excellent in low-temperature fixability, offset resistance, storage stability, and durability.

**SOLUTION:** A polyester resin binder for toner comprises a polyester resin having an intrinsic viscosity of 0.40 to 0.75. The alcohol component constituting the polyester resin contains 40 to 100 mol% of an aliphatic secondary diol having 2 to 4 carbon atoms. By using the polyester resin having the specified intrinsic viscosity and the specified proportion of the aliphatic secondary diol, the resulting toner exhibits a well-balanced fixing property and heat resistance, while maintaining good pulverizability and charging characteristics.

**EFFECT:** The polyester resin binder is suitable for producing an electrophotographic toner having improved low-temperature fixing performance and resistance to hot offset, together with excellent storage stability and image durability.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3
